bull_bear.body: Prioritizing reinvestment into FMCG innovation, digital supply chain, agri-value addition, and sustainability initiatives; no dividend or buyback details mentioned; focus on organic growth over debt-funded M&A.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Competition from FMCG giants (HUL, Nestle); input cost volatility in agri; regulatory scrutiny on tobacco-linked profits; scaling digital initiatives across rural India; execution risk in new product launches.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, purpose-driven, and future-focused; leadership emphasizes innovation, digital agility, sustainability as competitive moats, and long-term value creation over short-term gains.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: ITC’s agri-business is not a cost center but a strategic advantage — it provides proprietary, low-cost, traceable raw materials for FMCG, creating a defensible moat competitors cannot replicate without similar rural infrastructure.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Diversified conglomerate structure spanning FMCG (Cigarettes and Others), Agri Business, and Paperboards, Paper & Packaging, covering B2C, B2B and D2C segments
- Portfolio of world-class Indian brands in Foods, Personal Care Products, Education and Stationery Products, Matches and Agarbattis, together representing a consumer spend of over Rs. 37,000 crores
- Three-tier governance structure (Board strategic supervision, Corporate Management Committee strategic management, Divisional Chief Executives executive management) built on trusteeship, transparency, ethical corporate citizenship, empowerment & accountability and control
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Geopolitical and trade-policy volatility — Regional conflicts, evolving energy dynamics and tariff-led trade measures have heightened uncertainty in the operating environment, resulting in increased volatility across commodity and energy markets, disruptions in global supply chains, and a sharp escalation in logistics and ocean freight costs.
- Climate change exposure (physical and transition risk) — Given the Company's pan-India footprint and reliance on agricultural and forestry-based raw materials, it is inherently exposed to climate-related risks, including short-term impacts such as drought and erratic precipitation on its agri value chains, alongside longer-term transition risk from decarbonisation requirements across its own operations and value chain (Scope 1/2/3).
- Cyber security and IT-OT threat landscape — As the Company's digital transformation accelerates, it faces a rapidly evolving cyber-threat landscape spanning both information technology and operational technology (IT-OT) systems, requiring continuous strengthening of security architecture, monitoring and response readiness.
- Commodity and input-price volatility — Geopolitical disruptions have driven volatility in commodity and energy markets; the Company relies on long-term supply contracts, alternate fuels/materials, pipeline inventory management and structured hedging arrangements to mitigate commodity price risk and ensure continuity of operations.
- India/global macro deceleration and energy-security risk — The ongoing West Asia conflict has heightened concerns around India's energy security and imported inflation; a prolonged disruption, coupled with emerging El Nino conditions that could weaken monsoons and intensify heatwaves, poses risks to growth, inflation and the Current Account, with possible second-order impacts on consumer sentiment and demand.
- Foreign currency exposure — The Company's foreign currency exposures, arising from its cross-border operations and subsidiaries, are managed within the framework of Forex policies and procedures, indicating a structural currency-risk exposure inherent to its international footprint.
- Global supply-chain disruption and import dependency — Heightened geopolitical uncertainty has led to disruptions in global supply chains, prompting the Company to expand its sourcing and vendor base, diversify fuel and energy sources, develop alternate materials/formulations, and augment its domestic supplier base to enable import substitution.

business.body:
- Four disclosed business pillars on every page footer: "FMCG, PAPERBOARDS & PACKAGING, AGRI-BUSINESS, INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY"; the consolidated commentary names ITC Infotech India Limited, Surya Nepal Private Limited, Sproutlife Foods Private Limited and ITC Hotels Limited as group companies.
- Claims market standing across brands: 'Aashirvaad' Atta "continued to consolidate its leadership position across markets"; 'YiPPee!' Noodles "a strong No. 2 brand in Instant Noodles category"; 'Bingo!' "strengthening its market leadership in the Bridges segment"; 'Sunfeast Dark Fantasy' "leadership position in the premium segment"; Education & Stationery "further strengthened its leadership position".
- Fresh Food Business is framed as "a new vector of growth envisioned in the ITC Next strategy", leveraging "institutional strengths in Foods Science & Manufacturing, FMCG Food brands and Culinary expertise to capitalise on the burgeoning online food services segment".
- Agri Business is positioned as an internal moat, providing "strategic sourcing support to the Branded Packaged Foods and Cigarettes Businesses"; the Packaging & Printing Business likewise "continued to provide strategic support to the Cigarettes Business, enabling agile execution and accelerated turnaround for new launches".
- Corporate tagline slide: "ITC: Enduring Value — A passion for Profitable growth... in a way that is Sustainable... and Inclusive."
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Acquisition/Consolidation] "The Company on 1st April, 2026 acquired the right to nominate majority of the Directors on the Board of Sproutlife Foods Private Limited ('Sproutlife') and consequently, Sproutlife became a subsidiary of the Company with effect from the said date. In accordance with Ind AS 103 - Business Combinations, the Group remeasured its pre-existing interest in Sproutlife to fair value upon acquisition of control. The resultant gain on remeasurement has been disclosed under 'Exceptional Items'."
- [Tax] The Cigarettes Business is responding to an "unprecedented increase in tax" with a "strategic and calibrated response ... balancing the interests of all stakeholders"; the deck says "Strategy, execution and outcomes tracking well in line with internal plans".
- [Trade policy] Paperboards: "Minimum Import Price (MIP) on Virgin Multi-layer Paperboard extended till 30th September 2026" and "The Directorate General of Trade has recommended imposition of Anti-dumping Duties on supplies from Indonesia; pending approval from Ministry of Finance."
- [Integration] '24 Mantra' organic business: "Integration of the business was smoothly completed during the quarter, enabling realisation of synergy benefits going forward." FMCG margin commentary is repeatedly quoted "ex-Sresta".
- [Macro watch-outs] Deck flags "significant deficit in monsoon and lower Kharif sowing levels" (chart caption: "Rainfall at 16% deficit from LPA"), "emerging El Niño conditions", and West Asia conflict-driven crude/supply-chain disruption as key monitorables; FY27 Real GDP growth "expected at 6.4%" (Source: IMF WEO).

outlook.body: Expansion into high-growth adjacencies: ready-to-cook, immunity juices, organic food, B2B ingredients, frozen snacks; digital-first brands; scaling e-Choupal 4.0 to 10M villages; potential M&A in premium personal care or plant-based foods.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Paperboards & Specialty Papers Business: consolidate leadership position in the Indian Paper and Paperboards industry by leveraging recent investments in innovation platforms anchored on sustainable products and digital technologies to set new benchmarks in customer satisfaction, operational excellence and sustainability
- Packaging and Printing Business: sharpen strategic focus on innovation, customer-centric solutions, sustainability, capability building and smart manufacturing to reinforce leadership in integrated packaging solutions
- Packaging and Printing Business: continue to scale up Industry 4.0 adoption across units in line with its long-term roadmap
- Innovation pipeline anchored on the Company's Life Sciences & Technology Centre (LSTC), under the 'InnovPack' range, focused on molecular-science-led sustainable packaging solutions and transition to plastic alternatives (e.g. compostable barrier and recyclable coating systems)
- Leaf Tobacco (Agri Business): leverage deep customer relationships, crop development expertise, product quality, processing facilities and sustainability credentials to strengthen position as a reliable supply-chain partner for global customers
- For the financial year ended 31st March 2026, the Board recommended confirmation of an Interim Dividend of Rs. 6.50 per Ordinary Share of Rs. 1/- each and declaration of a Final Dividend of Rs. 8.00 per Ordinary Share, to be put to shareholders at the 115th AGM (23rd July 2026). No dividend-policy philosophy text, buyback, or debt-reduction intent statement was present in the routed sections beyond this year's dividend action.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Paperboards & Specialty Papers Business: entered into a Business Transfer Agreement (31 March 2025) to acquire the Century Pulp and Paper Undertaking ('CPP') of Aditya Birla Real Estate Limited at Lalkuan, Nainital, Uttarakhand — a paper-industry asset commissioned in 1984 with installed capacity of 4.8 lakh tonnes per annum — to add capacity at a new location as existing facilities are near saturation, add scale/economies, provide locational advantage for customer servicing and raw-material proximity, and enhance resilience through multi-site operations and portfolio diversification; the Competition Commission of India approved the acquisition on 16th December 2025. Specialty Papers segment saw robust growth in the year driven by capacity augmentation in Décor paper that was completed in FY 2024-25. The Business is pursuing a multi-tiered sustainable-products strategy to build plastic-replacement solutions: 'Platform 1' (recyclable, compostable and barrier-coated boards), 'Platform 2' (first-to-market fully recyclable Fusion boards replacing plastic 'foam' board) and 'Platform 3' (Moulded Fibre Products made from renewable natural fibres). To address long-term fibre security the Business is pursuing catchment expansion and productivity enhancement across plantations, plus structured engagement with policy stakeholders on collaborative plantation models. R&D is centred at ITC's Life Sciences and Technology Centre (LSTC) in Bengaluru, which has completed five decades of R&D and hosts a research community of over 400 scientists with a combined 4,000+ years of R&D/innovation experience. Investment in technologies improving environmental and social impact ('Specific R&D' and 'Specific Capex') constituted 19.2% of total R&D spend in FY26 (18.6% in FY25) and 16.8% of total capex in FY26 (28.7% in FY25).
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's macroeconomic outlook remains relatively resilient, supported by favourable agricultural prospects, steady services activity, Government's continued thrust on capital expenditure and supportive monetary and financial conditions; RBI projects Real GDP growth of 6.9% in FY 2026-27 (vs 7.6% in FY 2025-26)
- Rural consumption expected to be supported by resilient rural wages and declining unemployment; urban consumption expected to strengthen on measures boosting disposable incomes and a recovery in consumer credit
- Healthy corporate and bank balance sheets, low interest rates and capacity utilisation of approx. 75% provide a supportive foundation for a revival in private-sector capital expenditure
- Key near-term risks flagged: the ongoing West Asia conflict heightening concerns around India's energy security and imported inflation, and emerging El Niño conditions that could weaken monsoons and intensify heatwaves, with possible second-order impacts on consumer sentiment and demand
- Paperboards industry demand expected to be driven by favourable demographic trends, rapid urbanisation, a growing middle class, increasing substitution of plastic with sustainable alternatives, recently concluded FTAs and India's emergence as a global manufacturing hub, with strong growth anticipated from Pharmaceuticals, Apparel, QSRs/Food Service, FMCG, consumer durables and e-Commerce end-user segments; demand for Writing & Printing paper expected to remain firm on publishing and notebooks industry requirements linked to Government's education thrust
- Packaging industry outlook positive on rising disposable incomes, urbanisation, favourable demographics and increasing penetration of modern trade and e-Commerce; policy and regulatory initiatives strengthening food safety and organised retail expected to drive demand for high-quality, standardised packaging
- Growing stakeholder focus on decarbonisation and increasing regulatory emphasis on plastic reduction and circularity expected to accelerate adoption of sustainable packaging solutions, including recyclable, mono-material and circular alternatives
- Packaging and Printing Business has established a robust innovation pipeline under its 'InnovPack' range of sustainable packaging solutions, with multiple initiatives progressing through stages of customer validation and commercialisation

risks.note: Regional conflicts, evolving energy dynamics and tariff-led trade measures have heightened uncertainty in the operating environment, resulting in increased volatility across commodity and energy markets, disruptions in global supply chains, and a sharp escalation in logistics and ocean freight costs.

risks.risk: Climate change exposure (physical and transition risk)
risks.note: Given the Company's pan-India footprint and reliance on agricultural and forestry-based raw materials, it is inherently exposed to climate-related risks, including short-term impacts such as drought and erratic precipitation on its agri value chains, alongside longer-term transition risk from decarbonisation requirements across its own operations and value chain (Scope 1/2/3).

risks.risk: Cyber security and IT-OT threat landscape
risks.note: As the Company's digital transformation accelerates, it faces a rapidly evolving cyber-threat landscape spanning both information technology and operational technology (IT-OT) systems, requiring continuous strengthening of security architecture, monitoring and response readiness.

Geopolitical disruptions have driven volatility in commodity and energy markets; the Company relies on long-term supply contracts, alternate fuels/materials, pipeline inventory management and structured hedging arrangements to mitigate commodity price risk and ensure continuity of operations.

risks.risk: India/global macro deceleration and energy-security risk
risks.note: The ongoing West Asia conflict has heightened concerns around India's energy security and imported inflation; a prolonged disruption, coupled with emerging El Nino conditions that could weaken monsoons and intensify heatwaves, poses risks to growth, inflation and the Current Account, with possible second-order impacts on consumer sentiment and demand.

The Company's foreign currency exposures, arising from its cross-border operations and subsidiaries, are managed within the framework of Forex policies and procedures, indicating a structural currency-risk exposure inherent to its international footprint.

risks.risk: Global supply-chain disruption and import dependency
risks.note: Heightened geopolitical uncertainty has led to disruptions in global supply chains, prompting the Company to expand its sourcing and vendor base, diversify fuel and energy sources, develop alternate materials/formulations, and augment its domestic supplier base to enable import substitution.

one-line thesis: ITC is transforming into India’s most integrated FMCG player by leveraging its agri-sourcing moat, digital supply chain, and 25 mother brands to drive robust revenue growth and EBITDA margin expansion, while embedding sustainability as a core competitive advantage.

- Growing stakeholder focus on decarbonisation and increasing regulatory emphasis on plastic reduction and circularity expected to accelerate adoption of sustainable packaging solutions, including recyclable, mono-material and circular alternatives

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Acquisition/Consolidation] "The Company on 1st April, 2026 acquired the right to nominate majority of the Directors on the Board of Sproutlife Foods Private Limited ('Sproutlife') and consequently, Sproutlife became a subsidiary of the Company with effect from the said date. In accordance with Ind AS 103 - Business Combinations, the Group remeasured its pre-existing interest in Sproutlife to fair value upon acquisition of control. The resultant gain on remeasurement has been disclosed under 'Exceptional Items'."
- [Tax] The Cigarettes Business is responding to an "unprecedented increase in tax" with a "strategic and calibrated response ... balancing the interests of all stakeholders"; the deck says "Strategy, execution and outcomes tracking well in line with internal plans".
- [Trade policy] Paperboards: "Minimum Import Price (MIP) on Virgin Multi-layer Paperboard extended till 30th September 2026" and "The Directorate General of Trade has recommended imposition of Anti-dumping Duties on supplies from Indonesia; pending approval from Ministry of Finance."
- [Integration] '24 Mantra' organic business: "Integration of the business was smoothly completed during the quarter, enabling realisation of synergy benefits going forward." FMCG margin commentary is repeatedly quoted "ex-Sresta".
- [Macro watch-outs] Deck flags "significant deficit in monsoon and lower Kharif sowing levels" (chart caption: "Rainfall at 16% deficit from LPA"), "emerging El Niño conditions", and West Asia conflict-driven crude/supply-chain disruption as key monitorables; FY27 Real GDP growth "expected at 6.4%" (Source: IMF WEO).

one-line thesis: ITC is transforming into India’s most integrated FMCG player by leveraging its agri-sourcing moat, digital supply chain, and 25 mother brands to drive robust revenue growth and EBITDA margin expansion, while embedding sustainability as a core competitive advantage.
financial scorecard: Revenue: +16% YoY YTD FY21; EBITDA: +210 bps margin expansion YTD FY21; PAT: Not explicitly stated but implied strong due to margin growth; Orderbook: Not applicable; Net Debt: Not disclosed
guidance: No explicit forward guidance provided; emphasis on sustaining 16%+ revenue growth momentum and margin expansion through innovation, digital, and cost efficiencies.
segment / subsidiary detail: Foods: 12,844 cr revenue (FY21), #1 in branded atta, cream biscuits, snacks; Personal Care: Savlon, Dermafique; Stationery: Classmate #1; Matches & Agarbatti: #1 in Dhoop, #2 in Agarbatti; Agri: Largest wheat procurer after FCI, #1 in leaf tobacco exports; Value-added products: Organic spices, frozen prawns, dehydrated pulp, maida, besan.
growth verticals / optionality: Expansion into high-growth adjacencies: ready-to-cook, immunity juices, organic food, B2B ingredients, frozen snacks; digital-first brands; scaling e-Choupal 4.0 to 10M villages; potential M&A in premium personal care or plant-based foods.
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin expanded 460 bps over 3 years (FY17-FY20); driven by supply chain efficiencies, digital logistics, delayered operations, smart manufacturing, and direct-to-market shipments reducing distribution costs.
capex / expansion: Not explicitly stated; implied investment in ICMLs (Integrated Consumer Manufacturing Locations), smart manufacturing, e-Choupal digital infrastructure, and R&D (LSTC Bengaluru).
capital allocation: Prioritizing reinvestment into FMCG innovation, digital supply chain, agri-value addition, and sustainability initiatives; no dividend or buyback details mentioned; focus on organic growth over debt-funded M&A.
risks & watch-items: Competition from FMCG giants (HUL, Nestle); input cost volatility in agri; regulatory scrutiny on tobacco-linked profits; scaling digital initiatives across rural India; execution risk in new product launches.
management quality / tone: Confident, purpose-driven, and future-focused; leadership emphasizes innovation, digital agility, sustainability as competitive moats, and long-term value creation over short-term gains.
non-obvious takeaways: ITC’s agri-business is not a cost center but a strategic advantage — it provides proprietary, low-cost, traceable raw materials for FMCG, creating a defensible moat competitors cannot replicate without similar rural infrastructure.

themes.title: Consumption revival & FMCG premiumization
themes.need: Rural recovery, GST 2.0 and premiumization still frame the theme, but Q1FY27 rewarded portfolio SHAPE over volume. TATACONSUM's growth businesses hit INR 1,300cr (+47%) and are now 36% of India - larger than either salt (>INR 1,000cr) or tea & coffee (INR 1,200cr), with Sampann +58%, RTD +41% and Capital Foods INR 232cr (+40%) - while India tea revenue fell 4% on +2% volume as lower tea costs were deliberately passed back (tea inflation is now running 7-10% with most buying still ahead, so that inverts next year). PGHH shows the margin route: FY26 sales roughly flat at ~INR 4,300cr but PAT +19% to ~INR 850cr and ~100bps of structural margin from INR 86cr of productivity savings, absorbing crude and resin each up 30-50% with no stock-outs. The cautionary tale is licensed brands - JYOTHYLAB lost the Pril and Fa licences when Henkel did not renew (all manufacturing and selling stopped 1-June; Pril was ~7-8% of revenue, ~INR 225-240cr) and has filed SIAC arbitration. MARICO/DABUR/GODREJCP/COLPAL/EMAMILTD ride distribution + premium mix; VBL on beverage route-to-market; BIKAJI/GOPAL/BECTORFOOD on branded snacks; ORKLAINDIA took a 4% blended price increase in Q4 plus premium mix to a 16.9% EBITDA margin.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull-through; rural volume recovery; festive/wedding restocking; commodity pass-back timing; JYOTHYLAB's ~7-8% revenue hole and the SIAC arbitration.

hero.oneLiner: ITC is one of India's foremost private sector companies and a diversified conglomerate spanning FMCG (Cigarettes, Foods, Personal Care, Education & Stationery, Matches and Agarbattis), Agri Business and Paperboards, Paper & Packaging.
